mainTopic: The end of פרק עושין פסין (ביטול רשות of the house according to רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, and ערקבלין for מרור) and the opening משנה of בכל מערבין (which foods and places work for an עירוב).
overview: This amud opens at the end of a sugya. Two משניות seemed to contradict each other, and the answer is that one follows רבי אליעזר and the other follows the רבנן. רב ששת explains their dispute: for רבי אליעזר, someone who does ביטול רשות on his share of the חצר also gives up his house; for the רבנן, he does not. The גמרא asks why this needed saying (פשיטא). It answers with a case of five residents where one forgot to join the עירוב: for רבי אליעזר he need not give up his rights to each person separately, and a ברייתא saying this follows רבי אליעזר. A second version (רב טביומי's) attributes this connection to רב ששת himself. רב פפא then asks אביי what happens if a person openly says the opposite of each view's default, and אביי answers that a clearly stated intention always counts. The chapter closes with the משנה's teaching that ערקבלין may be used for מרור, ending פרק עושין פסין. A new chapter, בכל מערבין, begins: an עירוב may be made with any food except water and salt, and the food need only be fit for someone, with סומכוס and רבי יהודה adding their own views.

steps.title: The two sources follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction between the two משניות is solved: one follows רבי אליעזר, the other follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is רבי אליעזר, and that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a contradiction raised on the previous amud. It says the two משניות simply follow two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, two משניות seemed to disagree about what a person gives up when he does ביטול רשות. Instead of forcing them to agree, the גמרא assigns each to a different תנא. This is the standard 'two authorities' answer, and once it is used there is no real contradiction left.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... and that one. The formula for assigning two sources to two different opinions.
A תנא whose view is one side of this מחלוקת.
The Sages, the majority view that argues on רבי אליעזר.

steps.confusionAlert: This line answers a contradiction raised on the previous amud. It is not a fresh statement, so read it as the end of a contradiction-and-answer move.

phrases.english: This one is Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: The first משנה follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: and that one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The other משנה follows the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction between two משניות raised in the preceding text, on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תנאי היא: the two sources reflect two different תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seemed to give contradictory rulings on the same issue.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no contradiction. One משנה follows רבי אליעזר and the other follows the רבנן.

steps.title: The exact point of the מחלוקת: does the house go with the חצר?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains the dispute. According to רבי אליעזר, giving up the חצר includes the house. According to the רבנן, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you look closely, you will find this. According to רבי אליעזר, someone who gives up his rights in the חצר has also given up his rights in his house. According to the רבנן, someone who gives up his rights in the חצר has not given up his rights in his house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת defines exactly what רבי אליעזר and the רבנן argue about. It is the scope of ביטול רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 only told us that two opinions exist. Now we learn what they actually disagree on. For רבי אליעזר, renouncing the חצר automatically includes the house. For the רבנן, the house stays his unless he says otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: When you examine it closely, you will find. This introduces a precise analysis.
One who renounces his rights or authority. This is the mechanism used when someone did not join the עירוב.
His share of the shared courtyard.
His own house.
He has renounced.

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines how far ביטול רשות reaches. That matters in practice for where the other residents may carry on שבת.

phrases.english: When you examine it closely, you will find:
phrases.notes: These are the words of רב ששת.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Eliezer:
one who renounces his rights in the courtyard
has also renounced his rights in his house.
phrases.notes: The house goes along with the courtyard.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis:
one who renounces his rights in the courtyard
has not renounced his rights in his house.
phrases.notes: The house remains his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the content of the מחלוקת that step 1 relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר holds that ביטול of the חצר includes the house. The רבנן hold that it does not include the house.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב ששת's explanation adds nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת, saying his point is obvious. This sets up the next step, which will show why it was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know the two משניות follow two opinions, the point of disagreement seems clear without being spelled out. So why did רב ששת need to say it? The challenge is aimed at the necessity of the statement, not at whether it is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. A challenge claiming that a statement teaches nothing new.

steps.confusionAlert: פשיטא does not say רב ששת is wrong. It only asks why he needed to say something we already knew.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב ששת's statement in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The point of disagreement is already clear from step 1, so the explanation seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The case of five residents where one forgot the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רחבה, together with רב הונא בר חיננא, explains that רב ששת's point was needed for a case of five people in one חצר, one of whom forgot to join the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה said: רב הונא בר חיננא and I explained it this way. The statement was needed only for the case of five people living in one חצר, where one of them forgot and did not join the עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רחבה answers the פשיטא. He shows that רב ששת's explanation has a real purpose in a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the rule is not obvious in a case with many residents, where one person who forgot must do ביטול to several others. Something about having many residents might have made us think the rule works differently. The next part of the גמרא will explain what new point this case teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives this answer.
We explained it. Used for an interpretation.
It was needed only for. The standard answer to פשיטא, pointing to a specific case.
Dwelling or living, here meaning living in the courtyard.
He joined in the עירוב.

steps.whatToRemember: The two משניות follow רבי אליעזר and the רבנן. They argue whether ביטול of the חצר includes the house. This is not obvious in the case of five residents where one forgot to join the עירוב.

phrases.english: Rachava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא וְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא תַּרְגֵּימְנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinnana and I explained it:
It was needed only
for five people who live in one courtyard
and one of them forgot and did not join the eiruv.
phrases.notes: He must now renounce his rights to the other four. Step 5 explains what's new here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַחֲבָה: אֲנָא וְרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא תַּרְגֵּימְנָא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 3 by pointing to a specific case where the rule is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: לא נצרכא: limiting the statement to a specific case where it teaches something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's statement seemed obvious and unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement is needed for the case of five residents where one forgot to join the עירוב. Step 5 explains the novelty.

steps.title: Five people in one courtyard: does he have to give up his share to each one?
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the answer from Step 4. According to רבי אליעזר, the one who forgot does not need to give up his share to each person separately. According to the רבנן, he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, when he gives up his rights, he does not have to give them up to each and every person. According to the רבנן, when he gives up his rights, he must give them up to each and every person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 4. It shows the practical difference between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן in the case of five people sharing one חצר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a person who gives up his rights does it generously. That is why his ביטול includes his house too. For the same reason, we assume he gives up his share to everyone, even if he does not name each person. The רבנן do not assume this generosity, so he must give up his share to each resident explicitly.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving up one's rights in the shared courtyard, so the others may carry there on שבת
To each and every one, meaning separately to every resident
The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי אליעזר

steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the complaint in Step 3. רב ששת's explanation is not obvious, because it creates a real difference in how ביטול רשות must be done when there are many residents.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Eliezer:
when he gives up his rights,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צָרִיךְ לְבַטֵּל לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: he does not need to give them up to each and every one.
phrases.notes: He gives up his rights generously, so one general ביטול covers everyone.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis:
when he gives up his rights,
he must give them up to each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the content of the answer that Step 4 introduced
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a practical difference that comes out of רב ששת's explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's point seemed to add nothing new
steps.terutzMaskana: His point decides whether ביטול must be made to each resident separately

steps.title: Which opinion does the ברייתא about five residents follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says the one who forgot does not need to give up his share to each person separately, and asks whose opinion it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow? 'Five people who live in one courtyard, and one of them forgot and did not join the עירוב. When he gives up his rights, he does not need to give them up to each and every one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches the case just discussed and asks which opinion it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in the ברייתא, that he does not need to give up his share to each person, fits only one side of the argument laid out in Step 5. So the question really asks us to match the ברייתא to that side.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom does it go? This asks which opinion a source follows.
That was taught in a ברייתא
Living or residing
Joined the עירוב

phrases.english: According to whom is that which was taught:
Five people who live in one courtyard
and one of them forgot and did not join the eruv,
when he gives up his rights,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צָרִיךְ לְבַטֵּל רְשׁוּת לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: he does not need to give up his rights to each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the argument from Step 5 to a ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion, רבי אליעזר or the רבנן, the ברייתא follows

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? According to רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי אליעזר holds that ביטול is done generously, which is why one ביטול covers all the residents. The רבנן would require a separate ביטול for each person.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with רבי אליעזר

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, ביטול is done generously, so one ביטול covers everyone in the חצר. According to the רבנן, he must give up his share to each resident. The ברייתא about five residents follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6

steps.title: A second version of the passage asks the same question
steps.stepSummary: The way described so far is how רב כהנא taught the passage. רב טביומי taught it differently, and in his version the question about the ברייתא comes up again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא taught it this way. רב טביומי taught it this way: whose view does this ברייתא follow? 'Five people who live in one courtyard, and one of them forgot and did not join the עירוב. When he gives up his rights, he does not need to give them up to each and every one.' According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us there is a second way the passage was taught, and repeats the question about the ברייתא. This sets up a different answer in the next step, given by a different person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב כהנא's version, רחבה and רב הונא בר חיננא linked רב ששת's idea to the five-residents case. In רב טביומי's version, the link comes from רב ששת himself. The law does not change. Only the question of who said it changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught or transmitted (a version of the passage)
This way
The אמורא whose version was presented until now
The אמורא who taught a different version

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is quoted a second time on purpose. This is not a mistake or a new case. It is the same question, presented as part of רב טביומי's different version.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana taught it this way.
phrases.notes: He means the version just given, with רחבה and רב הונא בר חיננא.

phrases.english: Rav Tavyomei taught it this way:
According to whom is that which was taught:
Five people who live in one courtyard
and one of them forgot and did not join the eruv,
when he gives up his rights

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְבַטֵּל רְשׁוּת לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: he does not need to give up his rights to each and every one,
according to whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא מַתְנֵי הָכִי. רַב טַבְיוֹמֵי מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of how Steps 4 to 7 were transmitted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion the ברייתא follows, in רב טביומי's version

steps.title: רב ששת himself says the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: In רב טביומי's version, רב הונא בר יהודה reports that רב ששת said the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: according to whom? According to רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in the second version is the same, רבי אליעזר. The difference is that here it comes straight from רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר. In רב טביומי's version, רב ששת himself, as reported by רב הונא בר יהודה, connects the מחלוקת to the five-residents ברייתא. In רב כהנא's version, רחבה and רב הונא בר חיננא made that connection.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports רב ששת's statement
The אמורא who explained the argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן
'So-and-so said that so-and-so said,' a chain of transmission

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the ברייתא about five residents follows רבי אליעזר. The two versions disagree only about who made this connection: רחבה (רב כהנא's version) or רב ששת himself (רב טביומי's version).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said that Rav Sheshet said:
According to whom? According to Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8 within רב טביומי's version
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, as stated by רב ששת himself
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both versions agree on the law. They differ only about who said it.

steps.title: What if the person says the opposite of the default rule?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי two questions. According to רבי אליעזר, what if the person says 'I am not giving up my house'? According to the רבנן, what if he says 'I am giving up my house'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: According to רבי אליעזר, what if he says, 'I am not giving up my rights'? And according to the רבנן, what if he says, 'I am giving up my rights'? What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new question to אביי. It tests what happens when a person's spoken words go against what each opinion normally assumes. The next steps will lay out the possible sides of this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר assumes that giving up the courtyard (ביטול רשות) automatically includes the house. The רבנן assume it does not. רב פפא asks whether a clear statement from the person can override each opinion's default assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of אביי and רבא
I give up (renounce) my rights
I am not giving up my rights
What? (what is the law?)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the questions are 'flipped.' For רבי אליעזר the case is a person who says he is NOT giving up his house. For the רבנן the case is a person who says he IS giving up his house. Each case goes against that opinion's default.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אִי אָמַר: לָא מְבַטֵּילְנָא,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer, if he said: I am not renouncing (my house),
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר normally assumes the house is included

phrases.english: and according to the Rabbis, if he said: I am renouncing (my house) — what is the law?
phrases.notes: The רבנן normally assume the house is not included

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the מחלוקת defined in Step 2: whether ביטול of the חצר includes the house. It asks a new question about an explicit statement that goes against each view's default.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a person's explicit statement override each opinion's default assumption about whether the house is included in the ביטול?

steps.title: First possible reason for רבי אליעזר: it is only a guess about what he meant
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי אליעזר includes the house only because we assume that is what the person means. If he says clearly that he is not giving it up, then he keeps his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is רבי אליעזר's reason that he holds: one who gives up his courtyard rights, we assume he gave up his house rights too? If so, this person said clearly, 'I am not giving it up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first side of the question for רבי אליעזר. Maybe his rule is just an assumption about the person's intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר's rule is only a guess about what the person meant, then clear words beat the guess. Here the person openly said he is keeping his house, so he would keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
He holds / he is of the opinion
His rights in the courtyard
His rights in his house

phrases.english: Is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer because he holds:

phrases.aramaic: הַמְבַטֵּל רְשׁוּת חֲצֵירוֹ, רְשׁוּת בֵּיתוֹ בִּיטֵּל.
phrases.english: one who renounces rights to his courtyard has (presumably) renounced rights to his house.
phrases.notes: An assumption about the person's intent

phrases.english: And this one said: I am not renouncing.
phrases.notes: So his explicit words override the assumption

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first possible side of רב פפא's question about רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אליעזר's rule only a presumption about the person's intent, which an explicit statement can override?

steps.title: Second possible reason for רבי אליעזר: a house without a courtyard is useless
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe רבי אליעזר's reason is that people do not live in a house without a courtyard. If so, giving up the courtyard automatically gives up the house, and his words do not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps רבי אליעזר's reason is that people do not live in a house without a courtyard. So when he says 'I am not giving it up,' it is not in his power. Even though he says 'I will live there,' his words mean nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question for רבי אליעזר. Maybe the house is included because of a fact about how people live, not because of the person's intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reason, the house is tied to the courtyard because a house is not usable on its own. So the person's statement cannot change the outcome. His words are meaningless and the house is still included in the ביטול.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
People do not usually live (that way)
It is not in his power
He has said nothing (his words have no effect)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in the גמרא: the same rule can come from a guess about a person's intention, or from an objective fact. The difference shows up exactly when the person says the opposite.

phrases.english: Or perhaps the reason of Rabbi Eliezer
is because a house without a courtyard —
people do not usually live (in it).
phrases.notes: An objective fact, not about intent

phrases.english: And when he says: I am not renouncing —
it is not in his power,
even though he says: I will live (there) —
he has said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the competing reason to Step 11 for רבי אליעזר's view, which would lead to the opposite result.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אליעזר's rule based on an objective fact (a house is useless without a courtyard), so that the person's words cannot change it?

steps.title: The same question for the רבנן: the first possible reason
steps.stepSummary: Now the רבנן side. Maybe the רבנן say the house is not included only because we assume the person did not mean it. If so, a person who openly says he is giving up his house would succeed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, what if he says, 'I am giving it up'? What is the רבנן's reason? Is it because they hold that one who gives up his courtyard rights did not give up his house rights? If so, this person said clearly, 'I am giving it up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of רב פפא's question, about the רבנן. It begins with the possibility that their rule is just an assumption about intention. The other side of this question continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors Step 11. If the רבנן's rule is only a guess about what the person meant, then his clear statement that he is giving up his house should work. That would let the others carry into it.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold (plural of קסבר)
He did not renounce

phrases.english: And according to the Rabbis, if he said: I am renouncing.
What is the reason of the Rabbis?
Is it because they hold:
one who renounces rights to his courtyard —
has (presumably) not renounced rights to his house,
phrases.notes: An assumption about intent

phrases.english: and this one said: I am renouncing.
phrases.notes: So his explicit words should work

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבי אליעזר half of the question (Steps 11-12) to the רבנן half, beginning with the 'presumption of intent' side, parallel to Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רבנן's rule only a presumption about intent, so that an explicit statement of giving up the house would take effect?

steps.title: Maybe the רבנן hold that a person cannot give up his house at all
steps.stepSummary: This is the second side of רב פפא's question about the רבנן. Maybe people never leave themselves with no house and no courtyard, so saying 'I give up my house' would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe the reason of the רבנן is different. People do not normally remove themselves completely from both house and courtyard and become like a guest by their neighbors. If so, when this person says 'I am giving up my house,' his words have no power.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second half of רב פפא's question by offering another possible reason for the רבנן's view. It is still a question; the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 suggested the רבנן only guess what the person meant, so clear words would change the result. Here the opposite is suggested: the רבנן's rule is based on what people realistically do. If so, it overrides his words, and saying 'I give up my house' accomplishes nothing. This matches the structure of Steps 11-12 for רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
That he removes himself
A guest
I am giving up (my rights)
It is not in his power

phrases.english: Or perhaps, the reason of the Rabbis
is because a person does not usually
remove himself completely
from both house and courtyard,
and become like a guest among them.
phrases.notes: He would have no place of his own; he would be like a visitor with his neighbors.

phrases.english: And this one, when he says 'I am giving up' —
what he says is not in his power.
phrases.notes: His words do not take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the רבנן question begun in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רבנן's rule only a guess about intention, or a rule about human behavior that clear words cannot change?

steps.title: אביי answers: clearly stated intention always counts
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that in both רבי אליעזר's and the רבנן's views, once the person states his intention openly, his words decide the outcome.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Both according to the רבנן and according to רבי אליעזר, once he has revealed what he wants, it is revealed, and we follow it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers both of רב פפא's questions at once. Whatever the person clearly says is what happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of the dispute are only about cases where the person said nothing about the house. Under רבי אליעזר, saying 'I am not giving up my house' lets him keep it. Under the רבנן, saying 'I am giving up my house' works. So the first option in each question (Steps 11 and 13) is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Both according to the רבנן and according to רבי אליעזר
He revealed his intention

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן is only about what a person means when he doesn't say. If he states his intention clearly, everyone follows his words.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both opinions are default assumptions about intention, not fixed rules that override what a person says.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him (Rav Pappa):
Both according to the Rabbis and according to Rabbi Eliezer,
once he has revealed his intention — it is revealed.
phrases.notes: We follow what he clearly said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן בֵּין לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-part question laid out in Steps 10-14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In both views, a clear statement of intention decides the outcome. This confirms the 'assumed intention' reading (Steps 11 and 13).

steps.title: The משנה's teaching: ערקבלין can be used for bitter herbs on פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next teaching in the משנה, which רבי אלעאי heard from רבי אליעזר: one fulfills the מצוה of מרור on פסח with ערקבלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I also heard from him (רבי אליעזר) that one fulfills the obligation of bitter herbs on פסח with ערקבלין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up a question about one unfamiliar word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another of the separate teachings that רבי אלעאי reports from רבי אליעזר in the משנה. It has nothing to do with courtyards. It adds a plant to the list of acceptable bitter herbs for פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: And I also heard from him
One fulfills the obligation
A plant used as a bitter herb
Passover

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a link to the courtyard discussion. The משנה is simply listing several unrelated things רבי אלעאי heard from רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And I also heard from him
phrases.notes: רבי אלעאי speaking about רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: that one fulfills the obligation with arkablin on Passover.
phrases.notes: Meaning the obligation to eat bitter herbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁיּוֹצְאִים בְּעַרְקַבָּלִין בְּפֶסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the courtyard discussion and quotes a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One fulfills the מצוה of מרור on פסח with ערקבלין.

steps.title: What is ערקבלין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what plant the word ערקבלין refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is ערקבלין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of an unfamiliar word in the משנה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question about a word. Nothing is being challenged; the גמרא just wants to identify the plant.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is arkablin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the משנה quoted in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the plant called ערקבלין.

steps.title: ריש לקיש identifies ערקבלין
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that ערקבלין is אצוותא חרוזיאתא, a fiber that wraps around a date palm.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: It is אצוותא חרוזיאתא, a fiber that wraps itself around a date palm.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question by naming the plant in the Aramaic of his day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He swaps the unfamiliar word for a familiar local name. According to the Sefaria translation, it is a fiber-like growth that winds around a date palm. So this growth is acceptable as a bitter herb.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא of ארץ ישראל
A fiber that wraps around a date palm

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Atzvata ḥaruziyata.
phrases.notes: A fiber that winds itself around a date palm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ערקבלין is אצוותא חרוזיאתא, a fiber that grows around a date palm.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק עושין פסין
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line ends the chapter עושין פסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter עושין פסין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said when finishing a chapter. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again. The next chapter starts with a new משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you
Name of the chapter: 'One may make boards' around a well

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter ends with the last teaching רבי אלעאי heard from רבי אליעזר: one may fulfill the מצוה of מרור with ערקבלין, which ריש לקיש identifies as אצוותא חרוזיאתא. Just before that, the courtyard discussion concluded with אביי's rule that a clearly stated intention counts in both רבי אליעזר's and the רבנן's views.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One may make boards'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last discussion.

steps.title: Any food may be used for an עירוב except water and salt
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens the chapter: an עירוב or שיתוף may be made with any food, but not with water or salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We may make an עירוב and a שיתוף with anything, except water and salt.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new chapter begins with a new משנה. It states the basic rule that any food works for an עירוב or a שיתוף, but water and salt do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב needs real food, something that counts as a meal. Water and salt are not considered food that feeds a person, so they cannot serve as the עירוב. This one rule covers both kinds of joining: עירוב and שיתוף.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
We make an עירוב (joining courtyards or extending the תחום שבת)
We make a שיתוף מבואות (joining an alleyway)
Except for

steps.whyThisMatters: This sentence gives the chapter its name, בכל מערבין, and sets up the whole discussion of which foods qualify for an עירוב.

phrases.english: Mishna:
phrases.notes: Signals that a new משנה is starting; here it also opens a new chapter.

phrases.english: With anything one may make an eiruv and a shituf,
except for water and salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the closing line of עושין פסין in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any food may be used for an עירוב or שיתוף, except water and salt.

steps.title: The same exception for מעשר שני money and for one who vows off food
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds two parallel rules. מעשר שני money may buy anything except water and salt, and someone who vowed off food may still have water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anything may be bought with מעשר שני money, except water and salt. One who vows not to eat food is still allowed salt and water.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists two more areas of הלכה where water and salt are treated the same way. They are not counted as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני money may only be spent on food in ירושלים, so it cannot buy water or salt, since they are not considered food. In the same way, a נדר against "food" does not include water and salt, so the person may still have them. Grouping these together shows that water and salt are consistently treated as not being nourishing food.

keyTerms.meaning: Money that redeemed מעשר שני, which may only be spent on food in ירושלים
Is bought
One who makes a נדר (vow)
Food, nourishment

steps.confusionAlert: Water and salt are not forbidden to the person who vowed. The point is the opposite: his vow never covered them, because they are not counted as food.

phrases.english: And everything may be bought with tithe money,
except for water and salt.
One who vows off food,
is permitted salt and water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the water-and-salt exception from עירוב to two other areas of הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water and salt are not considered food: they cannot be bought with מעשר שני money and are not included in a נדר against food.

steps.title: An עירוב may use food the person himself cannot eat
steps.stepSummary: An עירוב may be made for a נזיר with wine and for a ישראל with תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may make an עירוב for a נזיר with wine, and for a ישראל with תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now teaches that the food of an עירוב does not have to be food that this particular person is allowed to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר may not drink wine, and a ישראל may not eat תרומה. Even so, the עירוב works, because the food is fit for other people: wine for a non-נזיר and תרומה for a כהן. The rule is that the food must be fit for someone, not necessarily for the person the עירוב serves.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow of נזירות and may not drink wine
Wine
The portion of produce given to a כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it

phrases.english: One may make an eiruv for a nazirite with wine,
and for an Israelite with teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which foods count to whose food counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב may be made with food that is forbidden to that person but permitted to others.

steps.title: סומכוס requires חולין for a ישראל
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס disagrees: a ישראל's עירוב must be made with חולין, not תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: סומכוס says: only with חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: A different opinion is recorded. סומכוס holds that a ישראל's עירוב must be made with ordinary food, not תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said food fit for anyone is enough. סומכוס disagrees in the case of a ישראל: since the ישראל himself cannot eat תרומה, it does not work as his עירוב. The גמרא will later clarify the exact scope of his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who often holds individual views
Ordinary food with no holiness, which anyone may eat

phrases.english: Summakhos says: With unconsecrated food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the תרומה part of step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to סומכוס, a ישראל's עירוב must be made with חולין.

steps.title: A כהן's עירוב may be placed in a בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows an עירוב for a כהן to be placed in a בית הפרס, even though the כהן normally should not go there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for a כהן, an עירוב may be placed in a בית הפרס.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to the place of the עירוב. It allows a כהן's עירוב to be placed in a field that may contain bits of bone from a grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן must avoid טומאת מת, and a בית הפרס is a plowed-over grave area where bones may be scattered. The משנה still permits his עירוב there. The גמרא will explain why the כהן can reach it, which is possible since the problem with a בית הפרס is only מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן, who must avoid טומאת מת
A field where a grave was plowed over, so bone pieces may be scattered; a doubtful area of טומאה

phrases.english: And for a priest, in a beit haperas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of עירובין made for people with personal restrictions, now about location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן's עירוב may be placed in a בית הפרס.

steps.title: רבי יהודה permits a כהן's עירוב even among the graves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה goes further and allows a כהן's עירוב to be placed even between the graves in a cemetery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: even between the graves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a stronger ruling. A כהן's עירוב may be placed even in an actual cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being among graves is a Torah-level problem for a כהן, which is more serious than a בית הפרס. Still, רבי יהודה permits it. The word "אפילו" shows he goes beyond the first opinion, and the גמרא will later explain how the כהן could reach it.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives a more lenient view here
Even; signals a bigger step than the previous ruling
Between the graves, in an actual cemetery

steps.whatToRemember: The opening משנה of בכל מערבין teaches three things. Water and salt are never "food." The food of an עירוב only needs to be fit for someone, which סומכוס disputes for תרומה. A כהן's עירוב may be placed in a בית הפרס, and רבי יהודה permits it even among the graves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even between the graves.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בֵּין הַקְּבָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 24 to a more severe location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a כהן's עירוב may be placed even among the graves.
